role.altitude: The gaming floor supervisor keeps checking money, judging staff, watching tables and talking to dealers and players; counting notes by hand, piecing together facts for evaluations, keeping a paper rotation chart and walking the floor to find empty hoppers shrink.
skills_to_grow: Using the rotation board and slot alerts
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who spends the shift on the floor with players and dealers, not on charts and counting.

tasks.short: Receive and check the customer's money, count it and exchange currency into the requested bills and coins, record the transaction, and hand over the money.

steps.what: Supervisor receives the customer's money and checks it for authenticity
Supervisor counts and exchanges currency into the requested combination of bills and coins
Supervisor records the transaction and the customer's identity above the legal threshold
Supervisor counts out the money to the customer

tasks.design: A note counter counts what the customer hands over, and a cash recycler dispenses the requested combination of bills and coins, so the supervisor checks the totals instead of counting each note twice by hand. Checking authenticity and counting out to the customer stay personal. Recording the transaction belongs to the transaction paperwork task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every exchange was counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Note counters and cash recyclers at the floor desk.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a customer splitting exchanges to stay under a threshold.

evidence.claim: Note counters and cash recyclers count and dispense requested denominations.
The gambling regulator supervises anti-money-laundering rules for land-based providers; unusual transactions are reported.

assumptions: Boundary: exchanging currency; paperwork for monetary transactions (task 23133) is a sibling task.
s3 is part of paperwork for monetary transactions, which sibling task 23133 covers; its saving is counted there.
Checking and handing over keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of exchanges at desks with a recycler.
research_questions: Do count differences at shift end fall?

incremental.description: Supervisor clears jams and reconciles the recycler at shift end.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few desks with recyclers; high: every exchange point equipped.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Gather facts on attendance, incidents and training, evaluate workers' performance, prepare the written performance evaluation, discuss it with the worker, and sign and file it.

steps.what: Supervisor gathers facts: attendance, incidents, training records and own observations
Supervisor prepares the written performance evaluation
Supervisor discusses the evaluation with the worker
Supervisor signs and files the final evaluation

tasks.design: The HR system shows the worker's absence record, training completed and logged incidents on one page, instead of collecting them from spreadsheets and files. Judging performance stays with the supervisor. The evaluation form lists the competencies with a scale and space for the supervisor's own words; no software rates or drafts the evaluation. After the conversation the signed form goes to HR in the system instead of on paper. Using attendance data in evaluations is agreed with the works council first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts sat in spreadsheets and paper files.
tasks.enabler_now: HR systems with staff overviews and evaluation forms.
tasks.still_hard: Workers whose shifts the supervisor rarely sees.
tasks.human_edge: Giving hard feedback that the worker accepts.
tasks.altitude: Less gathering; judging and the conversation stay.

reach.learn: Whether evaluations are complete and on time.

evidence.claim: AI that monitors or evaluates staff performance is high-risk, so no model rates or drafts here.
A time clock that can watch attendance or performance needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: evaluating performance and writing evaluations; training, supervising and scheduling (task 23156) is a sibling task whose evaluation part is this task.
Input contract for s1: absence, training and incident records kept in the HR system by HR and supervisors.
Judging and the conversation keep their full time.
unknowns: Whether incidents are logged per worker.
research_questions: Are evaluations completed on time more often?

incremental.description: Supervisor checks the staff overview for errors before use.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few records in the HR system; high: complete overviews per worker.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Circulate and monitor stations and games, check the dealer rotation, decide moves, and move dealers from game to game to ensure adequate staffing.

steps.what: Supervisor circulates and monitors stations and games
Supervisor checks the dealer rotation and breaks
Supervisor decides which dealer moves to which game
Supervisor moves dealers from game to game and tells them

tasks.design: A rotation board on a floor tablet shows which dealer is at which table, who is due for a break and which dealers are qualified for each game, and proposes the next break order by fixed rules, instead of a paper chart updated by hand. Watching the floor, deciding moves and telling dealers stay with the supervisor. The board uses skills and break times only, not dealers' behaviour.
tasks.previous_blocker: The rotation was kept on paper and in the supervisor's head.
tasks.still_hard: Sudden absences in the middle of a busy evening.
tasks.human_edge: Moving a dealer away from a tense table before it escalates.
tasks.altitude: Less chart-keeping; watching the floor stays.

reach.learn: Whether breaks are fairer and on time.

evidence.claim: A tool that allocates work by behaviour or traits is high-risk; rules on skills and break times are not.
Scheduling tools with skills, availability and conflict warnings exist for shift businesses.

assumptions: Boundary: moving dealers during the shift; deciding tables to open and scheduling staff (task 23150) is a sibling task.
Watching, deciding and moving keep their full time.

incremental.description: Supervisor taps each move into the board.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small floor; high: many tables and games.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Monitor functioning of slot machine coin dispensers, fill coin hoppers when necessary, record the fill, and check the dispenser after filling.

steps.what: Supervisor monitors slot machine coin dispensers on the floor
Supervisor records the fill on a fill slip with a witness
Supervisor checks that the dispenser works after the fill

tasks.design: The slot management system sends a hopper-low or hopper-empty alert with the machine number to the supervisor's handheld, so the supervisor goes to that machine instead of walking the floor to find it. Filling and checking stay hands-on. Recording the fill belongs to the transaction paperwork task and is priced there.
tasks.previous_blocker: Empty hoppers were found by walking the floor or by players calling.
tasks.enabler_now: Slot management systems with machine alerts to handhelds.
tasks.still_hard: Older machines not linked to the slot system.
tasks.human_edge: Spotting a jammed dispenser that the system reports as full.

reach.learn: Whether dispenser faults are reported sooner.

evidence.claim: Slot management systems alert staff when a machine's hopper runs low.

assumptions: Boundary: monitoring and filling hoppers; recording malfunctions (task 23138) and notifying technicians (task 23141) are sibling tasks.
s3 is the first record of the fill, signed in person with a witness; it keeps its full time.
Input contract for s1: about 80% of machines linked to the slot system; s1 is priced at that share.
Filling and checking keep their full time.
unknowns: Share of machines still using coin hoppers.
research_questions: Do machines stand empty for less time?

incremental.description: Supervisor acknowledges alerts on the handheld.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many machines not linked; high: most machines linked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
